::: {#rem-surprisal-fisher-information}
#### Surprisal and the Fisher information

When the probabilities depend on a parameter $\param$,
the surprisal of an outcome $x$ is $-\log \p(x \mid \param)$,
which is minus the log-likelihood.
Its derivative with respect to $\param$ is minus the
[score](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-score).
The expected squared score is the
[expected (Fisher) information](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-einf),
which is also the curvature of the Kullback--Leibler divergence
at the true parameter value
([proved in the sds notes](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#thm-fisher-kl-curvature)).
:::
